commit.message:
Simulate: report one commit's runs, and rewrite the script in Python

The results file keeps every run ever made, and both the summary at the
end of a sweep and --report counted all of them, so a failure from an
older commit read as a current one. Twice now that cost a look at a bug
that was already fixed.

A summary is now about one commit: the one a sweep just ran, or for
--report the current HEAD, including runs made with uncommitted changes
on top of it, which are labelled -dirty. --report --all shows every
commit in the file.

The script is Python now. It reads the file a line at a time, so a report
over a million runs takes seconds where the bash version ran sed over the
whole file three times and could not finish --all. Workers are threads in
one process, so appending needs no flock. An interrupt kills the running
simulators, drops their partial logs instead of recording them as
failures, and prints the summary of what did finish. The command line and
the JSON records are unchanged.

 
+The results file keeps every run ever made, so both the summary at the
+end of a sweep and `--report` show one commit's runs, and a failure from
+an older commit does not read as a current one.
+
 ### Watching it
 
 The same simulator has a terminal viewer. It draws the replicas on a ring

+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Runs the simulator with random seeds on every core until a time budget
+expires, or reports on the runs so far.
+
+Each run is a fresh seed, alternating between --lite and full swarm
+configurations. A run that exits non-zero or exceeds the timeout is a
+failure; its log is kept and its seed is printed so it can be reproduced.
+
+    scripts/simulate [--budget DURATION] [--timeout DURATION]
+                     [--concurrency N] [--out DIR]
+    scripts/simulate --report [--all] [--out DIR]
+
+Durations take the same suffixes as timeout(1): 30s, 10m, 2h.
+
+Results are appended as one JSON line per run to OUT/results.jsonl, with
+the commit, seed, mode, outcome, duration, and the command to reproduce.
+The file keeps every run ever made, so a summary only counts the runs of
+one commit: the one just simulated, or for --report the current HEAD,
+including runs made with uncommitted changes on top of it. --all reports
+every commit in the file.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import os
+import random
+import signal
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import threading
+import time
+from collections import Counter
+from pathlib import Path
+
+
+def parse_duration(text):
+    """Seconds for a timeout(1)-style duration: 30s, 10m, 2h, or plain seconds."""
+    units = {"s": 1, "m": 60, "h": 3600}
+    if text and text[-1] in units:
+        return int(text[:-1]) * units[text[-1]]
+    return int(text)
+
+
+def git(*args):
+    return subprocess.run(["git", *args], check=True, capture_output=True, text=True).stdout.strip()
+
+
+def current_commit():
+    """HEAD, with -dirty appended if the working tree differs from it."""
+    commit = git("rev-parse", "HEAD")
+    dirty = subprocess.run(["git", "diff", "--quiet", "HEAD"]).returncode != 0
+    return commit + "-dirty" if dirty else commit
+
+
+def read_runs(results, commit=None):
+    """The records in the results file, all of them or those of one commit.
+    A commit matches its own runs and those made with uncommitted changes on
+    top of it."""
+    if not results.exists():
+        return []
+    with results.open() as file:
+        runs = (json.loads(line) for line in file if line.strip())
+        if commit is None:
+            return list(runs)
+        return [run for run in runs if run["commit"].startswith(commit)]
+
+
+def summarize(results, commit=None):
+    """Prints the runs per commit and mode and the commands to reproduce
+    the failures. Returns whether every run shown passed."""
+    runs = read_runs(results, commit)
+    if not runs:
+        if commit is None:
+            print(f"no results in {results}")
+        else:
+            print(f"no runs of commit {commit[:7]} in {results}; --all shows every commit")
+        return True
+    if commit is None:
+        print("runs per commit and mode:")
+    else:
+        print(f"runs of commit {commit[:7]} per mode (--all shows every commit):")
+    counts = Counter()
+    for run in runs:
+        short = run["commit"][:7] + ("-dirty" if run["commit"].endswith("-dirty") else "")
+        counts[(short, run["mode"], run["ok"])] += 1
+    for (short, mode, ok), count in sorted(counts.items()):
+        print(f"  {short:13} {mode:4} {count:8} {'passed' if ok else 'FAILED'}")
+    failures = [run for run in runs if not run["ok"]]
+    print(f"total: {len(runs)} runs, {len(failures)} failed")
+    if failures:
+        print("reproduce with:")
+        for run in failures:
+            short = run["commit"][:7] + ("-dirty" if run["commit"].endswith("-dirty") else "")
+            print(f"  {run['command']}   (commit {short})")
+    return not failures
+
+
+class Sweep:
+    """Runs seeds on `concurrency` workers until the deadline."""
+
+    def __init__(self, binary, out, commit, timeout, deadline):
+        self.binary = binary
+        self.out = out
+        self.commit = commit
+        self.timeout = timeout
+        self.deadline = deadline
+        self.results = out / "results.jsonl"
+        self.lock = threading.Lock()
+        self.stop = threading.Event()
+        self.running = set()
+
+    def record(self, seed, mode, args, status, seconds):
+        ok = status == 0
+        record = {
+            "commit": self.commit,
+            "seed": seed,
+            "mode": mode,
+            "ok": ok,
+            "exit": status,
+            "seconds": seconds,
+            "command": f"cargo run --release -p vsr-simulator -- {' '.join(args + [str(seed)])}".replace("  ", " "),
+        }
+        with self.lock:
+            with self.results.open("a") as file:
+                file.write(json.dumps(record) + "\n")
+
+    def run_one(self):
+        seed = random.getrandbits(64)
+        mode, args = ("lite", ["--lite"]) if seed % 2 == 0 else ("full", [])
+        log = self.out / "logs" / f"{seed}.log"
+        start = time.monotonic()
+        with log.open("w") as file:
+            process = subprocess.Popen([self.binary, *args, str(seed)], stdout=file, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
+            with self.lock:
+                self.running.add(process)
+            try:
+                process.wait(timeout=self.timeout)
+                status = process.returncode
+            except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
+                process.kill()
+                process.wait()
+                status = 124
+            finally:
+                with self.lock:
+                    self.running.discard(process)
+        seconds = int(time.monotonic() - start)
+        if self.stop.is_set() and status != 0:
+            log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+            return  # killed by the interrupt, not a failure
+        command = f"{self.binary} {' '.join(args + [str(seed)])}"
+        if status == 0:
+            log.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+        elif status == 124:
+            print(f"TIMEOUT after {self.timeout}s: {command} (log: {log})", file=sys.stderr)
+        else:
+            print(f"FAILED (exit {status}): {command} (log: {log})", file=sys.stderr)
+        self.record(seed, mode, args, status, seconds)
+
+    def worker(self):
+        while not self.stop.is_set() and time.monotonic() < self.deadline:
+            self.run_one()
+
+    def interrupt(self):
+        self.stop.set()
+        with self.lock:
+            for process in list(self.running):
+                process.kill()
+
+
+def main():
+    # A report piped into head must end quietly.
+    signal.signal(signal.SIGPIPE, signal.SIG_DFL)
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
+    parser.add_argument("--budget", default="60m", help="how long to keep starting runs (default 60m)")
+    parser.add_argument("--timeout", default="10m", help="how long one run may take (default 10m)")
+    parser.add_argument("--concurrency", type=int, default=os.cpu_count(), help="parallel runs (default: cores)")
+    parser.add_argument("--out", default="target/simulate", help="results and logs directory")
+    parser.add_argument("--report", action="store_true", help="summarize the results so far instead of running")
+    parser.add_argument("--all", action="store_true", help="with --report: every commit, not just HEAD")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+
+    os.chdir(git("rev-parse", "--show-toplevel"))
+    out = Path(args.out)
+    results = out / "results.jsonl"
+
+    if args.report:
+        ok = summarize(results, None if args.all else git("rev-parse", "HEAD"))
+        sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)
+
+    subprocess.run(["cargo", "build", "--release", "-p", "vsr-simulator"], check=True)
+    (out / "logs").mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    commit = current_commit()
+    budget = parse_duration(args.budget)
+    sweep = Sweep(
+        binary="./target/release/vsr-simulator",
+        out=out,
+        commit=commit,
+        timeout=parse_duration(args.timeout),
+        deadline=time.monotonic() + budget,
+    )
+    print(f"simulating commit {commit} with {args.concurrency} workers for {args.budget} (timeout {args.timeout} per run)")
+    print(f"results: {results}")
+
+    threads = [threading.Thread(target=sweep.worker, daemon=True) for _ in range(args.concurrency)]
+    for thread in threads:
+        thread.start()
+    try:
+        for thread in threads:
+            thread.join()
+    except KeyboardInterrupt:
+        sweep.interrupt()
+        for thread in threads:
+            thread.join()
+        print("\ninterrupted", file=sys.stderr)
+        summarize(results, commit)
+        sys.exit(130)
+
+    print()
+    sys.exit(0 if summarize(results, commit) else 1)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
